pages.name: 0 · Opening Fiction—“What the Water Doesn't Take”

text.content: A 2,000–2,500-word story. It's the night of the theft seen through the eyes of Helen Ward (@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}): the podcast, the rain in Ballard, the flip phone with a single number, and someone who's already inside the apartment. It ends when Helen dials SAFE. David appears only as a voice on the phone. (There are two other possible points of view; see open decisions.)

• What this book is about
  • How to use this book: a chronicle for a coterie of 4–5 players, with David and Bear as allied NPCs (the doc 01 index said “for one player, with the coterie variant in a sidebar”)
  • Themes and mood: the city that records everything
  • Safety Tools: Lines and Veils, the X-Card, and the content warnings in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}
  • Quick Seattle glossary (neighborhoods, local slang, how the names are pronounced)

• Recent history: Whitmore's reign since the '70s, O'Connor's fall in 1978, the Gehenna War and what little remains of the Sabbat in Tacoma, the Anarch escalation in Everett, and the tech city as a new danger.
  • Political landscape: Prince, Sheriff, Primogen, Keeper of Elysium, and the Anarchs of the north.
  • Truths and lies: 12 rumors marked T/F/Half-true for the Storyteller.
  • Laws of the Seattle Elysium: 5 local traditions, among them “No connected device crosses the threshold.”
